tasks.title: Run installed bundle smokes in isolated native homes
tasks.goal: Build a reusable smoke harness that tests the exact prepared artifact on each supported native target.
steps: Extract the current native target list and archive/install route from existing distribution code; do not invent a target list or CLI flags.
For each target, unpack the subject-bound bundle into a fresh isolated home and invoke the installed executable through a harness port; retain target/runtime/bundle identity and bounded output.
Add native harness fixtures and a machine report for pass/fail/unavailable; foreign-host jobs remain unavailable until actually executed on that target.
positive_cases: Each available native target launches the exact unpacked binary.
Changing the installed artifact digest invalidates the smoke receipt.
negative_cases: Cross-compilation or a fake process cannot count as native execution evidence.
Unpack failure, wrong binary or nonzero execution is a failed/unavailable smoke, not pass.
checks: SELECT BEFORE DISPATCH: xtask target/cases are TO BIND from source/metadata to affected positive/negative obligations; choose --lib, --test <name>, --bin <name>, or affected --doc before compiling.

RUN BOUND CHECKS: after binding, use cargo test -p xtask <target> <case> -- --exact for lib/test/bin, or a reviewed small family without --exact; bind supported rustdoc selection separately. Verify intended nonzero cases in output; use target-specific --list only when needed to confirm selection, and reuse its valid inventory.

SELECT BEFORE DISPATCH: vibe-publish target/cases are TO BIND from source/metadata to affected positive/negative obligations; choose --lib, --test <name>, --bin <name>, or affected --doc before compiling.

RUN BOUND CHECKS: after binding, use cargo test -p vibe-publish <target> <case> -- --exact for lib/test/bin, or a reviewed small family without --exact; bind supported rustdoc selection separately. Verify intended nonzero cases in output; use target-specific --list only when needed to confirm selection, and reuse its valid inventory.

CONDITIONAL ORACLE: cargo xtask check-codegen only when the actual diff affects schemas, generators, generated-output registration or a dependent contract. Bind a narrower existing oracle if available; the global command needs that concrete impact and no adequate narrower check.

CONDITIONAL ORACLE: cargo xtask wire-diff only when the actual diff affects wire/format behavior, its corpus or epoch semantics. Bind a narrower existing oracle if available; the global command needs that concrete impact and no adequate narrower check.
cargo fmt --all -- --check
git diff --check
acceptance: All four native targets have distinct evidence rows; missing hosts remain outstanding obligations.
Harness proves actual installed artifact identity and leaves the real home unchanged.
tasks.safe_stop: Harness and runnable local smoke are ready; unavailable target evidence is explicitly pending.
tasks.commit_subject: feat(dist): smoke exact bundles in isolated native homes
notes: Native executors are supplied by the root task. Do not create CI infrastructure or acquire machines inside this task.

Schema changes: inspect the existing codegen entrypoint before regeneration; never hand-edit generated types or invent a new codegen command. The listed check-codegen and wire-diff oracles are conditional on the actual affected inputs, never on the allowed write perimeter alone.
Registration perimeter includes existing crate manifests and module owners only for required exports/dependencies; do not change unrelated declarations.

tasks.title: Make smoke default-on with explicit scoped skip
tasks.goal: Wire smoke policy into standalone preparation and its service reports without running full source tests implicitly.
steps: Add the explicit skip input to the existing preparation surface using the actual CLI grammar; route it through the shared service.
Bind requested target scope and skip reason/policy to a new prepared plan; keep pass/fail/skipped/unavailable distinct.
Ensure default failed smoke blocks readiness; explicit skip creates new evidence rather than editing a failed row; source tests remain separately requested.
positive_cases: An explicit skip produces a new plan with skipped status while still validating archive/subject identity.
negative_cases: Failed smoke never becomes passed by changing a presentation flag.
Skip does not omit identity checks, expand destinations or trigger source tests.
